newsitem.title: UK: Slovenia plans mark bond, syndicated loan, Samurai.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia plans mark bond, syndicated loan, Samurai.

text.p: Slovenia will launch a debut mark Eurobond within the next two weeks, Slovenian Finance Minister Mitja Gaspari told a news conference on Monday on the first day of investor presentations.
"This is a strategic transaction not an opportunistic one and we will use the proceeds to retire, restructure and replace our domestic debt," Gaspari said.
"The mark sector is the second most important market for us (after the dollar sector) and it is also important from a euro point of view," he added.
The Eurobond is likely to be around 300 million marks with a seven or 10-year maturity.
"But a 10-year deal is our preference," Gaspari said.
In terms of pricing the deal, he said Slovenia would like to achieve the tight spread achieved in its dollar deal.

Last July, Slovenia launched a debut Eurobond issue via J.P. Morgan. The $325 million five-year deal was priced to yield 58 basis points over U.S. Treasury notes, at the time the tightest spread for any Eurobond out of Eastern Europe. It was last trading around 47 b.p. over.

Credit Suisse First Boston's capital markets director Wolfgang Kerck said pricing of the mark bond would also depend on the outcome of the U.S. Federal Open Market Committee Meeting on Tuesday May 20.
He said the deal would be priced in line with Slovenia's credit ratings, the highest in Central and Eastern Europe.
Slovenia is rated A3 by Moody's Investors Service and A by Standard and Poor's. On Monday European credit rating agency IBCA said it may upgrade Slovenia from its current A-.
Bankers away from the lead have said Slovenia would have to pay a spread of LIBOR plus 25 basis points on a seven-year bond and Libor plus 35 b.p. on a 10-year bond.
"This (mark) bond will enable retail investors in Germany and Benelux to obtain a yield pick-up," Kerck said.
Dresdner Kleinwort Benson was appointed joint lead manager of the transaction.
Gaspari also said Slovenia will launch a syndicate loan in either dollars or marks in the late Autumn (October) and a Samurai bond early next year.
"Slovenia is the highest rated, most properous economy in Central and Eastern Europe," he said.
He said the government's key aims were to maintain fiscal balance, complete the privatisation programme, reform pensions, and European Union integration.
With regards to privatisation, he said the private sector would account for 65 percent of gross domestic product by the end of 1997.
The Slovenian delegation will visit Zurich on Tuesday and Frankfurt on Wednesday.
